items.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1960-09-03
items.q: Bill, with Ethel Waters, that series that they had on the radio. Oh, yeah, he was an actor.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Now, they had three legged sisters. One was married to Honest Whitman, you know, just to be, what did he play with Ethel Waters, Bill. They were from here, the legged sisters. They were popular show people that were married. One was married to Ernest Whitman.

items.title: Laurena Diggs and Carrie Boote Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: Because I know some of the leading, just like Ethel Waters. Ethel Waters, she worked in a street fair with a fellow named James Seymour.

ctx.x: I'm sort of jumping around today, but, uh, you say you had piano teachers? Did you have a voice teacher, too?

Me? No, no. Just, what little I tried was just something I, you know. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. they used to have organ grinders, you know, going around the street and you put the nickel and the man would play your piece. Well, most children save their nickels, you know, and when he'd come around, they'd get out there and dance up a breeze right on the street, you know. And there are so many children…
